text:
anya: Quick profiling dump from the overnight run — need help prioritizing. Short requests are blowing up p95 (prefill spikes), long requests push p99 (decode). 
malik: Can you paste the numbers or the flame? any kernel-switch points?
anya: Minimal slice: ```
prefill_mean_ms: 9.2
prefill_p95_ms: 28.7
prefill_p99_ms: 67.3
decode_mean_ms: 11.5
decode_p95_ms: 22.1
decode_p99_ms: 89.4
seq_len_break: ~128 (kernel A -> kernel B)
microbatch: median 4, tail 16-32
kv_hit_rate: 0.72 overall, 0.45 for new sessions
```
joel: Interesting — kernel flip at 128 matches where our matmul tiling changes. Small batches + kernel B for prefill seems costly for short seqs.
devon: We saw similar in the last perf-run: when microbatch <=4 kernel selection prefers a slower but more general kernel. For p95 targets we should bias prefill to the faster small-seq kernel even if decode keeps kernel B.
malik: KV cache misses look correlated with startups from certain regions — those are inflating prefill on p95 because prefill does large prefix attention. If kv_miss, prefill does full attention not cached.
rachel: Proposal: three short experiments — (A) force prefill->kernelA for seq<=256, (B) adaptive microbatch cap per-route (cap=4 for latency routes), (C) KV prewarm for top 5% prefixes. Small canaries for each.
anya: I like that order. Also we should split traces so prefill_ms and decode_ms are separate spans; current composite hides which stage contributes most per request.
joel: Agreed. Add a histogram of split latency by seq_len and microbatch size. We can generate a heatmap quickly from the perf traces.
devon: Quick note: forcing kernelA for prefill might reduce throughput by ~6% in steady-state due to lower packing efficiency; tradeoff is lower p95. We'll need to quantify throughput loss at system scale.
malik: For prioritization: 1) add split tracing (low cost, high signal). 2) run kernel-pin canary for prefill on a small fleet. 3) add per-route microbatch caps (config + rollout). 4) KV prewarm as a followup.
rachel: I'll open the PR for per-route caps and add flags to override kernel selection for prefill. Will add tests for seq thresholds and a feature flag.
anya: Also: consider a fast-path for short-seq requests that bypasses certain batching windows to avoid queuing jitter — microbatcher tweak.
joel: +1. That helps tail jitter from intermittent bursts.
sre-bot: perf-regression-alert: canary cluster alpha showed p95 +12% after kernel override experiment at 03:14 UTC, rolling back to previous policy.
devon: ack, reverting canary. We'll collect more instrumentation before re-trying.
malik: Action items / owners: split tracing -> joel; kernel canary plan -> devon + anya; per-route caps PR -> rachel; KV warm experiment -> malik.
anya: I'm going to write a short playbook for microbatch sizing decisions: default 8, latency routes 1-4, throughput routes 16-32, override when kv_hit_rate < 0.5. Will link after lunch.
rachel: tagging infra for capacity impact analysis. @infra FYI. :eyes:
anya: Thanks all — let's regroup after the first canary with split tracing enabled.
malik: I'll upload the heatmaps and a quick dashboard widget for prefill/decode split later today. :chart_with_upwards_trend:
